John Paul Jones plays the organ during a party aboard Led Zeppelin's tour plane. 1973.

In the suit is Ahmet Ertegun, co-founder and president of Atlantic Records, who first signed Zeppelin.

The plane, known as The Starship, was a former United Airlines Boeing 720 passenger jet. which was leased to several bands, including Led Zeppelin for their 1973 and 1975 North American concert tours. The interior was modified to reduce its seating capacity to forty and to install into the main cabin a bar, seats and tables, revolving arm chairs, a 30-foot-long (9.1 m) couch opposite the bar, a television set and a video cassette player, complete with a well-stocked video library. An electronic organ was built into the bar, and at the rear of the craft were two back rooms, one with a low couch and pillows on the floor, and the other, a bedroom, complete with a white fur bedspread and shower room. The exterior of the plane was re-sprayed with Led Zeppelin emblazoned down the side of the fuselage.

Other bands that used the plane included the Allman Brothers (who supposedly found "Welcome Allman Brothers" written on the planes bar in lines of cocaine once they boarded), Deep Purple, Frank Sinatra, Bob Dylan, The Band, Elton John, The Rolling Stones, Alice Cooper and Peter Frampton.
